blocks.text: The chapter presents restoration as an integrated whole: return to the land and its renewal are joined with cleansing from impurity and idols, concern for the LORD’s profaned name, a new heart and spirit, the gift of God’s Spirit, obedience, and later shame over past wrongdoing. These are not isolated promises; the chapter holds them together in its account of Israel’s restoration.

An ancient textual witness, Papyrus 967, places the material conventionally numbered Ezekiel 38–39 before chapter 37. This differs from the familiar Masoretic sequence and shows that the ordering of these later chapters was not identical in every ancient textual tradition.
